text:
The Griwick Compact endured eight years of internal fragmentation and external war, defined by a succession of six rulers who held the seat for an average of 1.1 years each. The period began with the murder of Throll Kell by Lorn Waldhith at Griwick in 44, a killing that allowed Tum Ga to seize the seat by the strongest claim. Tum Ga’s rule lasted only until Stonand Ker challenged and won in 45, taking the seat by coup and casting Tum Ga out. The Compact’s internal stability remained fragile; Lorn Waldhith was cast out in 45 for a conspiracy uncovered after two years, and Kou Peis was executed in 48 for a similar plot.

The Compact fought two wars against the Meigate Covenant, both won at Threi Cut in 47 and 48, with 12 and 10 dead respectively. These victories followed the Covenant’s declaration of war in 47 and its raid on Griwick in the same year, which carried off 23 grain and killed 16. The Compact sent one raid on Meigate in 45, which got through but took nothing. The war ended in 49 after two years of fighting, leaving both sides exhausted. During this time, the Compact suffered three raids from the Meigate Covenant: one on Griwick in 47, one on Laehiford in 49 that was beaten off, and one on Hadale in 51 that carried off 49 grain and killed 14.

Succession continued to shift rapidly. After Kou Peis murdered Stonand Ker in 47, Thres Thrild took the seat in 47, rejecting the rival claim of Drouldthas Stour, who was cast out. Raes Go took the seat by coup in 49 after challenging Thres Thrild, who was cast out. In 50, Paernmel Has challenged Raes Go openly, won, and took the seat, killing Raes Go at Griwick. Paernmel Has still held the seat when the period ended in 51. Throughout these years, 11 people were courted away from the ruler, and four people were cast out, reflecting a house coming apart from within.

The Wurn League’s fourteen-year span from 22 to 35 was defined by internal fragmentation and external defeat. At the start, the League was bound to the Kebarrow Compact through marriages in 23, 25, and 28, yet it suffered a raid by the Griwick Compact in 24 that carried off 34 grain and killed 16. The period ended with the League finished, its land lost and its followers scattered, following two decisive defeats by the Griwick Compact at Hadale in 33 and 34.

Internal instability drove the League’s decline. Nine people held the seat in this period, passing eight times. Trem Lolkoll was cast out in 26 after losing an open challenge to Gatros Hearn, who was then killed by Sothkel Sald. Sothkel Sald took the seat by coup in 26 but was killed by Saern Meastouth later that year. Saern Meastouth was cast out in 27 for attempted murder, allowing Teapeall Heampim to take the seat by right of birth. Teapeall Heampim died in 28, and Paernrom Sir took the seat by setting aside the claim of the named heir Bu Rumpirn. Paernrom Sir was murdered in 30 by Stonand Ker, who took the seat by coup in 33 after casting out Drarka Draernthun. Stonand Ker’s rule ended when his house ended in 34. Throughout this time, seven people were cast out and six of the League’s own people were murdered from within.

The League’s external position collapsed under pressure from the Griwick Compact. After declaring war in 33, the Griwick Compact defeated the League at Hadale, killing 58, and again in 34, killing 87. In 34, the Griwick Compact took Hadale from the League. The League’s three raids against the Griwick Compact at Vea Lode, Laehiford, and Threi Cut were all beaten off. The League was finished in 34, and peace was made with the Griwick Compact in 35.

The Griwick Compact’s twenty-year span from 4 to 23 was defined by a war with the Wurn League that lasted five years and ended in exhaustion, a succession crisis that shattered its internal cohesion, and a steady erosion of its authority that allowed places to rise against it. The period began with the Compact raiding Kebarrow, a move driven by famine at Vea Lode, and ended with Thold Valmaer holding the seat after a murder, having taken power by the strongest claim. Four people held the seat during this time, with an average tenure of 4.7 years and a median of 5.5. The seat passed three times: Pouldrir Ho was cast out, Kei Leassel died, Witrou Breim was killed, and Thold Valmaer remained in power at the end.

The conflict with the Wurn League began in 5 when the Compact declared war for Threi Cut and broke its alliance with the League. The League defeated the Compact at Threi Cut in 5, killing 45, but the Compact reversed this in 6 by defeating the League at the same site, killing 35. It won again at Threi Cut in 7, killing 29, and took Threi Cut from the League. In 8, the Compact took Laehiford from the League after defeating them there, killing 107, and defeated them again at Hadale in 9, killing 101. The war ended in 11 after five years, with both sides exhausted. Throughout the period, the Compact fought five battles against the League, winning four and losing one.

Internal stability collapsed in 9 when Pouldrir Ho was cast out for attempted murder. Kei Leassel took the seat by defeating the named heir Turaer Danpa, who was also cast out. The Compact’s standing fell very low, and Vea Lode rose against it in 9. By 12, its standing had fallen to nothing, and Threi Cut rose against it. Kei Leassel ruled until his death in 17. Witrou Breim took the seat by rejecting Beirn Naem’s claim, and Beirn was cast out. Witrou Breim was murdered by Bu Rumpirn in 23, and Thold Valmaer took the seat by the strongest claim. The Compact sent six raids, all carrying off plunder, and suffered ten raids, six of which were beaten off. Hunger killed 43 people across twelve years of famine.

The Kebarrow Compact’s nineteen-year tenure from 22 to 40 was defined by a relentless decline from a position of electoral authority to total dissolution. The period began with Sou Dra holding the seat, a ruler whose authority was immediately undermined by internal conspiracy and external aggression. The Compact’s standing eroded through a series of military defeats against the Griwick Compact, the loss of key territories, and the violent turnover of its leadership. By the end of the period, the power was finished, its land seized and its followers scattered.

Sou Dra’s rule was marked by instability and failed expansion. In 25, a raid on Griwick was beaten off, and a conspiracy by Turaer Danpa was uncovered, leading to Danpa’s execution. The Compact’s aggression continued in 26 with a successful raid on Laehiford, which brought 44 grain and killed 25, but this was met in kind when the Griwick Compact raided Kebarrow, taking 47 grain and killing 23. In 27, the Compact declared war on the Griwick Compact over a long-standing grievance, breaking a prior alliance. The war proved disastrous; the Compact was defeated at Vea Lode in 27 with 57 dead and again at Vea Lode in 28 with 48 dead. A raid on Threi Cut that year also failed to take anything. Sou Dra’s internal control slipped further as he ordered the murder of Thold Valmaer at Griwick in 28 and survived another conspiracy by Theald Va, who was executed.

The leadership of the Compact changed hands four times, each transition violent or forced. In 29, Tor Nathgoull challenged Sou Dra openly, won, and took the seat, casting Sou Dra out. Tor Nathgoull’s rule was short-lived; in 32, Throll Kell challenged him, won, and took the seat by coup, casting Tor Nathgoull out. Throll Kell held the seat until 35, when Beas Krouthea challenged him openly, won, and took the seat, casting Throll Kell out. Beas Krouthea’s rule ended in blood; in 38, Kou Peis murdered him at Kebarrow. During these years, the Compact suffered further losses. Meigate broke away in 29 to form the Meigate Covenant under Raes Go. A famine at Meigate in 26 had already killed 34 people. The Compact’s military fortunes remained poor, with raids on Hadale in 35 beaten off.

The final phase of the Compact saw it destroyed by the Griwick Compact. In 38, the Griwick Compact declared war on the Kebarrow Compact over a long-standing grievance. The Griwick Compact and its allies defeated the Kebarrow Compact at Kebarrow in 38 with 142 dead. Diweith Mound took the seat by election in 38 following Beas Krouthea’s death, but his rule was brief and treacherous; he attempted to murder Durnrin Drar in 39 and was cast out for attempted murder. The Griwick Compact and its allies defeated the Kebarrow Compact at Kebarrow again in 39 with 118 dead, then took Kebarrow from the Compact. The Kebarrow Compact was finished, landless, with its last 9 followers scattering. The Griwick Compact and the Kebarrow Compact made peace in 40, after the collapse of the Kebarrow Compact.

The Kebarrow Compact’s twenty-year span from 2 to 21 was defined by internal instability and external predation. The period began with a marriage binding the Compact to the Griwick Compact, but this alliance offered no protection against the raids that soon followed. The seat passed through five rulers, with power shifting violently between them. Three rulers were killed, one was cast out, and one remained in office at the end. The Compact’s standing fluctuated, suffering a notable rebellion when its authority had fallen very low, yet it continued to launch raids despite frequent failures.

Reweld Wul took the seat in 8 after Searn Sisrill was killed by Math Ham. His rule ended when Witrou Breim had him murdered in 14. Witrou Breim then took the seat by election, but his tenure was short-lived. In 15, Pouldrir Ho challenged him openly, won, and took the seat. Witrou Breim was cast out and later declared outlaw after a conspiracy was uncovered. During this time, the Compact’s raids were mixed in success; it carried off plunder from Laehiford in 4 and 13, but its raid on Hadale in 6 was beaten off. The Compact suffered raids from the Griwick Compact and the Wurn League, losing grain and lives at Kebarrow and Meigate.

Pouldrir Ho’s rule ended in 20 when Turaer Danpa had him murdered. Sou Dra took the seat by election in 20 and held it through the end of the period. Thra Bround challenged Sou Dra openly in 21 but lost and was killed. Throughout the period, four exiles returned to serve the Compact, and four people were courted away from its ruler. One year of hunger at Meigate killed 23 people. The Compact sent eight raids, three of which were beaten off and two of which took nothing. It suffered six raids, all of which carried off plunder except for two that took nothing. The period ended with Sou Dra still holding the seat.

The Wurn League’s twenty-year span from 2 to 21 was defined by a rapid collapse of its external alliances and a catastrophic loss of territory to the Griwick Compact. The period began with the League occupying Threi Cut and binding itself to both the Kebarrow Compact and the Griwick Compact through six marriages. It ended with the League holding only its original seat, having lost Threi Cut and Laehiford, and having fought five battles against Griwick, winning only one. The internal stability of the League was equally fragile, with three rulers holding the seat in succession, two of whom were removed by force or death.

At the start, the League sought security through kinship, marrying Witrou Breim to Beirn Naem and Teapeall Heampim to Thra Bround in year 3, followed by three more unions in years 4 and 5. This diplomatic web unraveled in year 5 when the Griwick Compact declared war over Threi Cut and broke its alliance. The League’s response was mixed: it defeated Griwick at Threi Cut in year 5, killing 45, but suffered a raid on Laehiford by the Kebarrow Compact that carried off 29 grain. The League retaliated by raiding Kebarrow and Meigate, but took nothing in either instance. The conflict with Griwick escalated in year 6, when famine killed 13 at Threi Cut, and Griwick defeated the League at Threi Cut, killing 35.

By year 7, the League had lost Threi Cut to Griwick after another defeat. Internal strife erupted when Reweld Wul attempted to murder Searn Sisrill and was cast out. Math Ham then contested the claim of the named heir Witrou Breim and took the seat, casting out Witrou. Math Ham’s rule was violent; he had Searn Sisrill murdered at Kebarrow in year 8 and raided Griwick, killing 45. Griwick responded by raiding Hadale and defeating the League at Laehiford, taking the settlement. The League lost Laehiford in year 8 after a defeat that killed 107, and lost Hadale in year 9 after another defeat that killed 101. Math Ham was killed by Kei Leassel at Hadale in year 10.

Trem Lolkoll took the seat by right of birth in year 10. The League and Griwick made peace after five years of war. Trem Lolkoll’s rule saw the League’s raids on Vea Lode, Threi Cut, Laehiford, and Griwick all beaten off. Nael War returned from exile in year 18. The period ended with Trem Lolkoll still holding the seat, the League having lost two places, and its alliances largely dissolved, though a final marriage to the Kebarrow Compact was made in year 20.

The Griwick Compact’s twenty-year span from 24 to 43 was defined by violent succession, territorial expansion, and the collapse of its rivals. The period began with a coup that installed Bu Rumpirn, who was immediately challenged and cast out by Thold Valmaer. Valmaer ruled until his death in 28, after which Nael War took the seat by the strongest claim. The Compact fought six battles, winning all of them, and expanded its territory by taking Hadale from the Wurn League and Kebarrow from the Kebarrow Compact. It suffered two major plagues that killed 640 people and caused 510 to flee. The era ended with Throll Kell holding the seat after an open challenge, while the Wurn League and Kebarrow Compact had been destroyed.

Thold Valmaer and Bu Rumpirn exchanged the seat in 24 through successive coups. Valmaer was cast out, then won back the seat, only to be killed by Sou Dra in 28. Nael War took the seat by the strongest claim. The Compact engaged in a war with the Kebarrow Compact starting in 27, defeating them at Vea Lode in 27 and 28. Peace was made in 29. The Compact also fought the Wurn League, defeating them at Hadale in 33 and 34, and taking Hadale in 34. The Wurn League was finished in 34. Kondruth Tru took the seat by the strongest claim in 34 after Nael War was killed by Stonand Ker.

The Compact faced internal instability and external threats. Throll Kell returned from exile in 36. Kondruth Tru was killed by Beas Krouthea in 37. Durnrin Drar took the seat by the strongest claim. Laehiford rose against the Compact in 37. Durnrin Drar was murdered by Stonand Ker in 41. Heth Fal contested the claim of Sor Pean and took the seat in 41, casting out Sor Pean. Throll Kell challenged Heth Fal openly in 42, won, and took the seat. The Compact raided Vea Lode in 42. The period ended with Throll Kell holding the seat.

The Vea Lode Covenant began in year 29 when Vea Lode broke from the Griwick Compact, with Mothgall Vafarn taking the seat. The new power faced immediate hardship, as a famine at Vea Lode in year 30 left grain short and 11 dead. The crisis deepened in subsequent years, with the famine persisting through year 33. In year 31, 13 more died and 32 abandoned the place. In year 32, 9 died and 22 left. In year 33, 7 died and 30 abandoned the place.

Internal strife followed the external pressure. In year 33, Sou Dra had Mothgall Vafarn murdered at Vea Lode. Sou Dra then took the seat of the Vea Lode Covenant by election. The Covenant turned outward, raiding Griwick in year 34, carrying off 36 grain and killing 20. In year 35, it raided Laehiford, carrying off 44 grain and killing 28.

Bu Rumpirn, who had returned from exile in year 30, acted against the ruler. In year 36, Bu Rumpirn had Sou Dra murdered at Vea Lode. Bu Rumpirn took the seat by election. He ruled until he died at 60 in Vea Lode in year 39. The Vea Lode Covenant came to an end in year 39; its 1 place fell to no one.

The Meigate Covenant’s twenty-three years from 29 to 51 were defined by a shift from isolation to entanglement, and finally to exhaustion. It began by breaking from the Kebarrow Compact in 29, with Raes Go taking the seat. The period opened with a series of failed raids against the Griwick Compact and the Kebarrow Compact, all beaten off. A famine at Meigate in 38 killed 61 people and left grain short by 7. The Covenant’s standing fluctuated as it occupied Vea Lode in 41, only to lose it to a rising in 45 when its standing had fallen to nothing. Raes Go was cast out in 44 after losing an open challenge to Diweith Mound, who was himself killed in 46. Drarka Draernthun took the seat that year, setting aside the claim of the named heir Tor Nathgoull.

The Covenant’s external relations turned volatile. It declared war on the Griwick Compact in 47 over a long-standing grievance, breaking its alliance with them. The Covenant raided Griwick, carrying off 23 grain and killing 16, but was defeated at Threi Cut later that year with 12 dead. It was defeated again at Threi Cut in 48 with 10 dead. Peace was made in 49 after two years of war, leaving both sides exhausted. A marriage between Hehum Skul and Ta Poveil in 50 bound the Meigate Covenant to the Griwick Compact. Throughout the period, the seat passed from one person to another two times. Three people held the seat: Raes Go, Diweith Mound, and Drarka Draernthun. One was cast out, one was killed, and one was still holding.

Internal stability was undermined by repeated exiles and returns. Eleven exiles returned to take service with the Meigate Covenant during these years. Three people were courted away from its ruler: Heillvar Maer won Nourn Dem away in 41, Heillvar Maer won Drarka Draernthun away in 42, and Drarka Draernthun won Kaes Rou away in 46. Hunger afflicted Vea Lode multiple times, killing 68 people in all and causing 60 to flee their homes. The Covenant sent eight raids, four of which were beaten off and four of which carried off plunder. It suffered two raids from the Griwick Compact. The period ended with the Meigate Covenant still holding the seat, having fought two battles, both lost to the Griwick Compact.

Paernmel Has took the seat of the Griwick Compact in year 50 by openly challenging and defeating Raes Go. He killed Raes Go at Griwick later that same year. Tor Nathgoull was raised to steward of the Griwick Compact in year 50.

In year 51, Visal Veill married Treild Haen at Hadale. Paernmel Has’s child, Gim Raeldrol, was born at Kebarrow in year 51. Voudreirn Wer, Trurkeand Busi, and Ta Poveil each won Bakrei Dea away from the ruler of the Griwick Compact in year 51. The Griwick Compact spent 205 silver buying goodwill for the fifth time in year 51, and was not believed.

The Meigate Covenant raided Hadale in year 51, carrying off 49 grain and killing 14. The period ended in 51 with Paernmel Has still holding the seat.

Drarka Draernthun took the seat of the Meigate Covenant in 46 after winning an election that set aside the claim of the named heir Tor Nathgoull. The seat had passed from Diweith Mound, who was killed by Stonand Ker at Meigate earlier that year, to Drarka. Tor Nathgoull was cast out as the losing claimant. One person, Kaes Rou, was courted away from Drarka in 46. The period ran for 6 years, ending in 51 with Drarka still holding the seat.

The Meigate Covenant began a war against the Griwick Compact in 47 over a long-standing grievance, breaking its alliance and trade with them. The Covenant lost two battles to the Griwick Compact at Threi Cut in 47 and 48, with 12 and 10 dead respectively. It sent out three raids: one against Griwick in 47 carrying off 23 grain and killing 16; one against Laehiford in 49 that was beaten off; and one against Hadale in 51 carrying off 49 grain and killing 14. Peace was made after 2 years of war in 49. Five exiles returned to take service during the period.

Hunger at Vea Lode lasted 3 years, passing in 46, and struck again in 51, killing 1 and causing 20 to flee. A marriage in 50 tied the Meigate Covenant to the Griwick Compact. Drarka’s child Threarnvi Teas was born in 50. The rule ended in 51 with Drarka still holding the seat.

The war began in 27 when the Kebarrow Compact declared it on the Griwick Compact over a long-standing grievance. The Griwick Compact defeated the Kebarrow Compact at Vea Lode in the same year, with 57 dead. The Griwick Compact defeated the Kebarrow Compact at Vea Lode again in 28, with 48 dead.

In 28, Sou Dra had Thold Valmaer murdered at Griwick. The Kebarrow Compact and the Griwick Compact made peace in 29 after 2 years, both sides exhausted.

The Griwick Compact declared war on the Wurn League in year 5, seeking control of Threi Cut. The Wurn League defeated the Griwick Compact at Threi Cut in year 5, with 45 dead. The Griwick Compact defeated the Wurn League at Threi Cut in year 6, with 35 dead. The Griwick Compact defeated the Wurn League at Threi Cut in year 7, with 29 dead. The Griwick Compact took Threi Cut from the Wurn League in year 7.

The Griwick Compact defeated the Wurn League at Laehiford in year 8, with 107 dead. The Griwick Compact took Laehiford from the Wurn League in year 8. The Griwick Compact defeated the Wurn League at Hadale in year 9, with 101 dead. The Griwick Compact and the Wurn League made peace in year 10 after 5 years, both sides exhausted.
